title: Runtime profile issuance with signature rotation and shadow verification
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: Verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) are currently published as static artifacts. Over time profiles can become stale due to kernel updates, quantization changes, or different traffic distributions. We need an issuance process that provides cryptographic provenance, periodically rotates signing keys, and includes a lightweight production shadow-verification step before republishing a refreshed profile.

Goal: Implement a profile issuance pipeline that: 1) produces signed profile artifacts with metadata provenance, 2) supports scheduled signature key rotation with an auditable ledger of previous keys, and 3) runs a shadow-verification pass that samples live traffic (safe, redacted) to validate profile assumptions prior to public republish. This should reduce accidental rollouts of degraded performance and make rollbacks faster and more confident.

Scope: This ticket covers the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and stakeholder signoff for the issuance + rotation + shadow-verification flow. Engineering tickets (ENG-4821, ENG-4877) will implement the runtime and signing infra; Design will update the Console publish flow.

Out of scope: Full on-prem HSM integration (handled in Private deployment track), long-term archival retention policy for old keys (separate compliance effort).
acceptance_criteria: Signed profile artifact format specified (JSON manifest + detached signature) and documented in Confluence
Key rotation API defined: create/retire public keys, with backward compatibility for verification during a 30-day overlap
Shadow-verification flow implemented: sample <=1% of production requests (PII redacted) and run lightweight microbench to check latency and token cost deltas
Console UX: profile publish flow shows signature status, last-rotation, and shadow-verification pass/fail with links to sample traces
Rollback playbook defined and automated: if shadow verification fails or post-publish alerts trigger, system auto-tags profile as quarantined and triggers canary rollback
Telemetry: baseline and post-refresh latency/cost deltas are recorded to dashboards and surfaced as a release health metric
tasks: Draft formal artifact schema and signature verification rules (PM -> spec)
Coordinate with Security on KMS/HSM rotation policy and zero-trust access
Add shadow-verification toggle and safety limits (max sample %, PII strip rules) to runtime
Design Console publish modal with signature metadata and verification summary
Define canary sample cohorts and automatic quarantine thresholds
Prepare release notes and runbook for SRE and support teams
comments: 2025-01-17 - Arjun: Spiked schema options: embedding an attestations array vs. detached signature. Leaning toward detached sig so manifests remain readable and easier to stream-verify.
2025-01-22 - Dana: Security okayed detached signatures; asked for explicit key overlap period and revocation list. Adding 30-day overlap in acceptance criteria.
2025-01-30 - Eng (Diego Martinez): ENG-4821 bootstrapped a signing service prototype using KMS-backed keys. Need PM to finalize artifact fields for 'runtime_anchor' and 'profile_fingerprint'.

2025-02-04 - Arjun: Updated spec draft and added sample redaction rules per legal feedback. Shadow samples must remove message text and only include token-level timing/cost metrics + truncated prompt hash.

2025-02-14 - Dana: Design feedback received from Priya (Console): show last successful shadow-verification timestamp and quick 'rerun verification' button. Also call out any sample population bias warnings.

2025-02-28 - Arjun: Aligning rollout: staggered region publish for EU first, then NA, to limit blast radius. Drafting communication to customers for planned short maintenance window for EU profile republish.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow sampling could leak PII if redaction rules miss edge cases. Mitigation: legal-approved redaction rules + sampling run in isolated environment and only token-metrics retained.

Risk: Key rotation could invalidate old published clients that still verify against older keys. Mitigation: 30-day overlap and publish a rolling trust-anchor bundle; console will show deprecation schedule.

Risk: False positives from microbench diffs leading to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use median + 90th percentile thresholds and require both latency and cost regressions to exceed thresholds before quarantine.
notes: We intentionally separate artifact signing from hosting: signed manifests can be mirrored to multiple CDNs while verification uses the public key registry hosted in the Console.
This flow is designed to be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments; Private will have a later ticket to wire HSM key material into local signing endpoints.
Follow-up: schedule a tabletop incident drill with SRE to exercise the quarantine/rollback playbook once ENG work completes.
